actions.reason: C0001 has a coherent RNA-defined biological identity with strong down-regulation of metabolic and secretory pathways (large effect sizes, low q-values). WXS and CNV are not significant but do not actively contradict the RNA signal. Technical confounders are not specifically enriched in this set. Cross-modal consistency is weak but not contradictory, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0001 for downstream validation is better supported than Drop.

C0002 shows moderate but coherent support from RNA (up-regulation of beta cell and heme metabolism pathways) and CNV continuous features (multiple significant features with moderate-to-large effect sizes), with a suggestive PBRM1 mutation enrichment. Technical confounders are not specifically enriched. Cross-modal consistency is moderate (WSI and RNA positive). Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. The identity is sufficiently defensible for retention.

C0003 lacks coherent identity evidence: only one RNA pathway is significant, WXS and CNV show no significant enrichment, and the rare CNV events are based on very few cases with wide confidence intervals. Cross-modal consistency is weak, with some patients not supported by any modality. No technical confounder is specifically enriched, but the absence of positive biological identity and lack of structural support for Split or Merge make Drop better supported than Accept.

C0004 has no significant RNA pathway enrichment, and WXS/CNV findings are suggestive but not robust after FDR correction. Cross-modal consistency is weak, with no patient having all modalities positive and low internal structure reproducibility (resample ARI 0.532). No technical confounder is specifically enriched, but the lack of coherent biological identity and absence of positive structural evidence for Split or Merge make Drop better supported than Accept.

C0005 has no significant biological enrichment in RNA, WXS, or CNV, with all q-values near 1.0. The strong CT silhouette is likely explained by the significant technical confound with CT manufacturer and reconstruction kernel, which provides a substantial alternative explanation for any imaging-derived signal. Cross-modal consistency is weak outside CT. The absence of coherent biological identity and the dominant technical confound make Drop better supported than Accept.

C0006 has a strong, coherent biological identity defined by RNA (down-regulation of myogenesis, up-regulation of inflammatory/interferon pathways with low q-values) and significant BAP1 mutation enrichment (large effect size, q=0.017). Technical confounders are not specifically enriched. Cross-modal consistency is moderate-to-good (RNA and WSI positive, high patient support). Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0006 for downstream validation is better supported than Drop.
